reviewer: sql_security; independent of the focal author/executor
method: File-only review of CSV, all package hashes, real worker and exact test/config, all35 source hashes including33 frozen Git files, every retained assertion and financial snapshot hash. No imports/tests, network, Native, app or database commands executed by reviewer.

originalContract.precondiciones: FixtureCP1-24; proveedor acepta mensaje pero conexión pierde acuse
originalContract.pasos: Restaurar fixture; aplicar la entrada una vez, salvo reintento explícito; observar respuesta y estado persistido; comparar con oráculo independiente.
originalContract.resultado_esperado: Movimiento único; la entrega física tras timeout es incierta. Registrar esa limitación; el código no garantiza exactly-once de Telegram ni conciliación automática.
originalContract.evidencia_requerida: Proveedor doble registra recepción y timeout; logs política de recuperación

originalCases.basis: The provider double durably records acceptance in its retained event log before throwing the synthetic acknowledgement-timeout error. The actual worker records delivery unconfirmed, releases the lease, retains the durable event and schedules retry. Closing/reopening the persistent PGlite database then replaying the same financial request returns the same receipt. Retry confirms a second modeled physical acceptance while the economic rows remain identical.

sourceBinding.sqlScope: One baseline plus27 real migrations; not30 SQL files or35 migrations.
replacementBoundaries: The bounded query adapter substitutes PostgREST transport while executing realSQL and actual claim/release RPCs under the synthetic service role.
Platform/Auth roles and linked chat are a synthetic fixture, not a normal GoTrue session.
Only sendTelegramDm is mocked; its first accepted callback throws an immediate synthetic timeout, not an observed external socket timeout.
sourceBinding.testDiscovery: Explicit archived .test-source.ts focal config, one additional test afterCI6; not added to the913-test aggregate.

limits: The two acceptance receipts are generated by a controlled callback double. They model ambiguous delivery and a possible duplicate; they do not establish realTelegram delivery or external provider behavior.

No exactly-once physical message delivery or automatic provider reconciliation is asserted. This is not the distinct failure where provider acknowledgement succeeds but the database acknowledgement fails.
Only the new own event available_at is advanced to exercise retry. No worker policy, OS clock or financial row is changed for that scheduling control.
No native stack/GoTrue/Next/browser or concurrent-cron acceptance is inferred. Those contracts remain separate.
